title: What is known about 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1LC1RF_0RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1LC1RF_0RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
It is one of a pair, 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1L?1RF_0RB---, that differ only in E0 (here 1LC, there 1LD). The outer sweeps never read E0, so the two machines share them; the inner phases differ.
verdict: The question is open. The outer sweeps are proved in Lean, but the inner phases, which decide how the blocks grow, are only observed; no invariant that would exclude a halt is known.

Where a halt would have to come from. The machine halts only in F reading a 1. F is entered only from E reading a 1, and E only from D reading a 0; so a halt needs the head in D on 0 1 1 (and as D is entered only from A reading a 1, the head in A on 1 0 1 1). F is entered constantly (in the regular sweeps), 343,472,060 times in 2·1010 steps, and always reads a 0: the cell after …0011 is always the start of 0101….

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 84,091 cells have been visited and 40,430 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Single-token sweeps
claims.text: Moving right, B turns c = 1101010 into 0011001 and a = 10 into 01; moving left, C crosses an a (shifted by one cell) unchanged.

claims.title: The outer sweep pair
claims.text: With the head in C on the leftmost cell and the tape 11010 w (10)k+2 1, one round trip gives 11010 c w (10)k+1 1, in 24·#c(w) + 4·#a(w) + 4k + 41 steps. Proved for every w with up to four blocks of c's: w = cn, cn ax+1 cm, and so on, for all exponents.

claims.title: From the blank tape to the first outer phase
claims.text: After 12262 steps the tape is 11010 w (10)k 1 with w = c a27 c a8 c a2 c, k = 43.

claims.title: The sweep rule holds for every w seen
claims.text: Every arrival at the left end in the first 4·10<sup>8</sup> steps whose last block has k ≥ 2 is followed by the sweep pair above, with the exact step count, whatever w is: 3,216 sweep pairs, no exception.

claims.title: F always reads 0
claims.text: In 2·1010 steps state F is entered 343,472,060 times, always on a 0; no halt. The context is always …0011 F>0, followed by 101… or by cells not yet visited.

claims.title: Inner phases
claims.text:
When the last block is used up the head stops reaching the left end for a long time. claims.title: Why it is hard
claims.text: The inner phase is a smaller machine of the same kind working on the right end of the tape: short sweeps move one a at a time from one block into a longer one, so blocks get multiplied rather than added. Each outer phase takes time about quadratic in the tape length, and each inner phase produces a much longer last block, so the phases grow quickly and nothing in sight closes the loop.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts only if the head is ever in D on 0 1 1; it never was in 2·1010 steps.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine sweeps back and forth across a tape made of two words, and every round trip moves a little of the last block to the front; when the last block runs out, a long phase of shorter sweeps rebuilds the tape bigger. This page runs the real machine in your browser; the round trips are proved in Lean.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
The outer round trip is a theorem (up to four blocks).
F is entered 343,472,060 times, always on a 0.

sections.heading: A tape of two words
html: Each time the head comes back to the left end of the tape (in state C, on the leftmost cell) the tape reads 11010 w (10)k 1, where w is a word made of c = 1101010 and a = 10. Moving right, the head turns every c into 0011001 and every a into 01; moving left it turns them back, shifted.

sections.heading: Round trips move the last block to the front
html: One round trip takes one a off the last block and puts a new c at the front:

The middle of the tape is untouched. This is proved in Lean for every w with up to four blocks of cs and all block lengths, and the simulation finds no exception for any w. So an outer phase lasts as many round trips as the last block has as, and the front block of cs grows by that many.

sections.heading: When the last block runs out
html: When the last block is used up (it then eats the last c as well), the head stops returning to the left end. A long inner phase of shorter sweeps runs near the right part of the tape. It moves as one at a time between neighbouring blocks, multiplying their lengths, and leaves a new, much longer last block. Then the outer phase starts again.

The two machines of the pair differ only in E0, which the outer sweeps never read; they differ in the inner phases. Halting needs the head in D on 0 1 1. F, the state before a halt, is entered all the time (343,472,060 times in 2·1010 steps), but always on a 0.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495).
After 109 steps the tape spans 84,091 cells (9,731 left of the start, 51,091 right), with a density of 1s of 0.481.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: sweeping c/a-word counter with multiplying inner phases (1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1L?1RF_0RB--- pair)
summary: Outer phase: full sweeps over a tape 11010 w (10)^k 1 (w a word over c = 1101010, a = 10) each move one a from the last block into a new c at the front, proved in Lean; when the last block is used up, a long inner phase of short sweeps rebuilds and lengthens the blocks. F is entered all the time but always reads 0.
